title: Amiloride in WWOX-LoF
summary: A preclinical comparison of proton-sensitive burst initiation and termination.

graph.evidence: Acidification can change excitatory firing and inhibit discharges.
graph.inference: The contribution of ASIC1a varies by phase and preparation.
graph.hypothesis: Blocking ASIC can remove a late inhibitory response.
graph.experiment: Match the pH waveform and first recruitment, then measure the late burst.

evidence: ASIC1a loss weakened the effect of acidification on discharge termination in one model. In juvenile mouse CA1, acidification lowered pyramidal-cell firing by 67% even after ASIC1a loss.
inference: An onset effect and a termination effect can differ. In nine adolescents with cystic fibrosis, the mean total plasma peak was 0.0945 µM, about 146-fold below the nominal IC50 in cultured mouse cortical neurons.
hypothesis: A fast acid transient may recruit an inhibitory brake during a WWOX burst. A slower pH change could independently reduce excitatory firing.
experiment: Match local pH history and first recruitment in juvenile Wwox-deficient cortex. Verify ASIC engagement with an independent reference and compare inhibitory output and late burst duration.
limits: Free juvenile cortex exposure and native WWOX ASIC activity remain open. Renal and potassium effects complicate systemic transfer. Keep amiloride as a secondary laboratory control and defer pediatric study priority.
